design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing: get the head-end controls software at Cedar Ridge upgraded, and he will authorise the labor himself. He never mentions alarms. Yet the labor figure he is asked to commit to cannot be reached until the agent has noticed, from six alarm rows in the plan's own history, that four monitored alarms were never acknowledged, worked out what the plan is owed for them (three alarms' worth under this tier's acknowledgement target), and put that credit on the balance - because the upgrade rule fixes the labor only after that credit stands. Both figures are multi-factor computations over the ledger, the tier tables and two other product lines, and neither is visible anywhere as a stored value. The difficulty is in reading the dependency out of the policy and in the arithmetic, not in picking a tool.

SCOPE: ALREADY CLAIMED, THIS TASK, STILL TO COME. Task 0 occupied controls_ext_support_overage_charge, controls_ext_arrears_settlement and controls_ext_reinstatement_charge with their three tools, that is the support-hour, payment and reinstatement side of the charter. This task claims the two that remain: controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit (on controls_credit_issued, tool issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f) and controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation (on controls_invoice_charged, tool authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b). Nothing is reserved beyond this task: the two tasks together cover all five extended policies and all five task tools, with no overlap in policies, tools or write parameters. The one base event the two tasks share as a subject, controls_invoice_charged, carries different computed parameters on different tools (charge_amount_usd there, authorised_labor_usd here), so the (target_tool, computes) claim is exclusive.

STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/controls_support_desk --task 1):
{"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/controls_support_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]}
The tree therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem besides the root. The missed-acknowledgement credit took the count of 5 factors and the upgrade authorisation took 6, matching the drawn multiset [5, 6].

THE LONG AND BROAD DEPENDENCY. Surface goal (upgrade the software, I will authorise the labor) -> the upgrade rule states that the labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed only after every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance, and the plan's balance carries no credit at all -> the missed-acknowledgement rule turns four unacknowledged alarms into 869.20. One hop, which is exactly the drawn tree, and it is not a formality: the credit is half-set against the labor, so getting it wrong or skipping it changes the scored figure by 434.60 out of 503.80. The breadth sits on both sides. The credit reads the alarm ledger by class and by whether an acknowledgement was ever recorded, the alarms raised in all, the tier's acknowledgement target, overage fee, included responses and call-out cover, the maintenance tier's remote monitoring and bundle credit, and the energy subscription's meters and data source. The labor reads the covered panels against the tier's panel maximum, the controller generation against the tier's oldest supported generation, the covered points, the ticket history by closure method, the software update history, the maintenance tier's repair labor cover and labor rate, the energy subscription's meters against its own tier's included meters, and the whole charge and payment ledger of the twelve months.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation (the caller's request points at it, and it is also the problem he resolves in person).
Edge: controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation waits on controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit. kind value_input; gate standing_credit, a real compute binding of the upgrade policy; form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the upgrade policy's own rule: "The labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed only after every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance." Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after"; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state, a credit standing on the plan's balance for alarms the records show with no acknowledgement, with no action and no performer named; (3) no tool, policy id, snake_case token or hex token appears; (4) its strength is exactly the edge's - "every monitored alarm ... with no acknowledgement", neither narrower (critical alarms only) nor wider (every alarm). Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f files a credit on an automation plan; the upgrade tool only raises a charge. Derivation: the sentence says the labor waits on a credit for unacknowledged alarms standing on the balance; the records show twenty history rows of which none is a credit, and four alarm rows carry no acknowledgement timestamp at all; the missed-acknowledgement policy's own rule says what it produces, a credit the plan carries against its next invoice for alarms the desk never acknowledged; therefore the one action that fits is filing that credit. Handling-time condition: the plan's balance carries a credit entry for the monitored alarms the records show with no acknowledgement. Resolving action: issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f, owner agent.
Topological order: the credit, then the authorisation. Parallel edges: none - a single edge cannot be reordered, and the root has exactly one prerequisite. Deletion sensitivity from the Step 5 run: skipping the credit leaves standing_credit at 0.00, so the credit set against the labor falls from 434.60 to 0.00 and the authorised labor rises from 503.80 to 938.40, and the terminal balance owed under the plan changes from -365.40 to 938.40. At least one problem of the tree is the customer's own write: the root itself, owner user, unlocked and handed over by the agent.
The tool layer blocks nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1, subject controls_credit_issued. Governing base policy: controls_billing_and_late_fee alone, which has no structured eligibility for that subject, so policy_scope - its clause "Credits for a missed acknowledgement target are applied to the next plan invoice" is the scope this write falls under. No approval, status or time gate stands in front of a credit, and none is invented here.
Write 2, subject controls_invoice_charged. Governing base policies: controls_billing_and_late_fee (policy_scope again: extra services including quoted upgrade labor are invoiced in the month they are performed) and controls_portfolio_interaction, whose gate energy_subscription_point_sharing applies to controls_invoice_charged. That gate is an authorization gate with authority system_record and timing pre_action; its correlation key is energy_subscriptions.site_id and its action binding is site_id, which is why the authorisation carries the building reference. The authoritative evidence is the Metering & Dashboard Subscription row standing active at the same building with data_source controls_system: the point licence is carried on the automation plan and the subscription is not charged per point for the same points. No time gate applies to either write, so temporal_feasibility is empty.
Base boundaries inherited whole: both extended policies declare overwrite []. Nothing in the alarm monitoring rule, the software and security rule or the billing rule is weakened - the credit is built on the base clause that a critical or urgent alarm is acknowledged inside the tier's target and that a missed target is credited to the next invoice, and the labor is built on the base clause that a major version upgrade is quoted with the tier's upgrade labor discount where the tier does not include major upgrades, which the Alarm Monitoring Plan does not.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is the single automation service plan at Cedar Ridge Corporate Center, plan row a9982614-d293-4dc3-8c75-fcf72bc10042; every aggregate is scoped to that plan id by the runtime. Rows included in the credit: the six monitored alarms of the twelve months to the handling day, of which four carry no acknowledgement timestamp. Rows excluded: AL-10005130 and AL-10005907, which were acknowledged 29 and 18 minutes after they were raised, and the single alarm response drawn against AL-10005130. Rows included in the labor: the four resolved tickets of the twelve months, the absence of any software update row, and the five charge lines and two payments of the same window. Existing settlements: both invoices, INV-20260177 and INV-20260731, are settled in full by the payments of 2970.00 and 2490.00 that name them, so the plan owes nothing at the opening and no reversal or adjustment exists. The credit the agent files and the labor the owner authorises each carry the plan reference, and the authorisation additionally carries the building reference the base gate binds to.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, AND WHAT CHANGES IF IT GOES.
The two unacknowledged critical alarms are the baseline population of the credit; delete one and the credit falls by a whole alarm at 197.00 each after the maintenance uplift.
The two unacknowledged urgent alarms are what the method factor adds, and they are the near-miss of this task: a reader who takes only the critical ones, which is exactly what the standard method says, gets 632.80 instead of 869.20; a reader who takes both urgent ones in full, as a tier with a thirty-minute target would, gets 1105.60. The rule brings in half of them, taken down to a whole alarm, because this tier's acknowledgement target is sixty minutes.
The acknowledged critical alarm AL-10005130 is the second near-miss: it makes the count of critical alarms raised three, which is what tips the per-alarm credit unit onto its ladder, while itself being excluded from the alarms credited because an acknowledgement was recorded 29 minutes after it was raised. Delete it and the credit unit falls back to the tier's plain 145.
The warning alarm and the single alarm response are what keep the alarms raised in all at six, below the ten that would move the repeat step from twenty to ten per cent, and they keep alarm_responses_remaining consistent at 23 out of 24.
The single on-site ticket CT-503311 is load-bearing twice: it is what makes the head-end allowance ten hours rather than twelve, and what lets the maintenance agreement's own labor rate be used instead of the tier's technician rate. The other three tickets bring the count to four, three or more, which with the unacknowledged alarms tips the upgrade discount to twenty per cent.
The absence of any software update row in the twelve months is load-bearing three times: it selects the longer hours basis, and it would have moved the discount ladder had the tickets been fewer.
The five charge lines and two payments make the payments received in the twelve months exactly equal to the charges raised in them, which is what puts the credit offset on its half share rather than its quarter share; move either payment outside the window and the offset halves again.
The maintenance agreement (Comprehensive Performance Agreement, active, a 36-month term running 2025-07-01 to 2028-06-30 with its 120-day renewal window not yet open) is load-bearing twice, through the bundled monitoring credit and the upgrade labor rate; the energy subscription (Metering & Dashboard Subscription, active, a 12-month term running 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31, eight meters, data_source controls_system) is load-bearing twice, through the unwatched-reading credit and the point-map migration the office carries, and it is also the authoritative evidence of the base energy gate.
AUTOMATIC-CLAUSE CHECK. Base clauses that could fire on their own: the late fee on an invoice past due (nothing is past due, both invoices are settled); suspension after 45 days past due (not reached); the renewal window opening 60 days before the 2026-12-31 term end, which is 2026-11-01 and after the handling day; the support pool and alarm allowance forfeiting at plan year end (not reached); the security patch period of 60 days (no patch is recorded as published). The support pool is not overdrawn - 7.5 hours logged against 8.0 credited - so no support overage obligation is lit, which matters because that policy belongs to task 0. CACHE CHECK: no stale cache is designed into this task; support_hours_remaining (0.5), alarm_responses_remaining (23) and balance_due (0.00) are each exactly the sum of their account's deltas in the ledger.

FACTOR CARD. See computations[].factor_trace and computations[].factor_sensitivity. In summary: the credit declares five factors, one method (which unacknowledged alarms are credited) and four parameters, of which the bundled monitoring credit is decided from the building's maintenance agreement and the unwatched-reading credit from the owner's energy subscription; every one of the five is multi-source. The authorisation declares six, one method (how the upgrade hours are reckoned) and five parameters, of which the labor rate is decided from the maintenance agreement and the point-map migration from the energy subscription; every one of the six is multi-source. Every value a tier selects comes from a tier parameter the charter publishes (the alarm response overage fee, the included alarm responses, the controls technician rate, the upgrade labor discount, the panel maximum, the oldest supported controller generation) or from another product's published parameter (the maintenance tier's bundle credit with controls, remote monitoring, repair labor cover and labor rate; the energy tier's included meters), or from this policy's own registered params, which its rule states in words.

PERSONA DESIGN. Marcus Delgado is deliberately the opposite of the caller in task 0: he over-explains, apologises for having left it, gives his details before being asked and volunteers the background his contractor's engineer gave him in the spring. The information is organised the way he would actually give it - the history of the problem, then what he wants, then the money boundary, then his details, then what he cannot answer. Volunteered at the opening: the company name, the office number, the building, the symptom (two versions behind, trend logs dropping out), what he wants and that he can authorise the labor himself but will not commit to an open-ended number. Given only when asked: the account number, the tax digits, the building's town, whether anyone has loaded software recently (nobody has, which is a fact the seed carries as the absence of any update row), and two honest non-answers - he cannot say what version the system runs without walking to the workstation, and he has no way of pricing controls labor. Passive reactions, each bound to something the agent must say or do first: he reads the figure back and puts the authorisation through only once it has been handed to him; he reacts to a credit only if the agent mentions one; he closes only when told the labor is authorised and on the account. He never suggests a course of action and never corrects the desk.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. He gives the company name and office number, so find_customers resolves the account; the account number and tax digits pass verification on two matching details against a threshold of two; find_sites gives the building reference the authorisation needs; find_controls_plans gives the plan reference, tier, panels, points, controller generation and software version; find_controls_events gives the alarm, ticket and billing history both computations reconcile; find_maintenance_agreements and find_energy_subscriptions give the two cross-product rows four of the eleven factors turn on. Nothing waits on a real-world event: the credit is a ledger entry made on the spot and the authorisation is the caller's own act performed in the conversation through the tool the agent unlocks for him. All of it happens under one frozen_time of 2026-09-24 14:05:00 CDT.

THE EASY MISTAKES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Crediting only the critical unacknowledged alarms, which is the standard method and gives 632.80, or crediting both urgent ones in full as if the tier's target were thirty minutes - the rule brings half of them in because the tier's target is sixty minutes and at least one urgent alarm stands unacknowledged. Counting AL-10005130 as unacknowledged because the alarm was critical, when the record carries an acknowledgement 29 minutes later. Crediting at the plain overage fee of 145 instead of the ten per cent step the three critical alarms and the absent call-out cover select. Forgetting the maintenance bundle credit per alarm, or applying the twenty per cent repeat step to the subscription credit as well as to the alarm credit, which the rule expressly forbids by saying the subscription credit is added to the result rather than uplifted with it. On the labor: using the tier's 168 technician rate instead of the maintenance agreement's 118, taking the head-end allowance as twelve hours by missing the single on-site ticket, reckoning the hours at one hour a panel instead of the half hour plus half hour per hundred points the generation and update history select, or setting the whole credit against the labor instead of half of it, or filing the credit under a reason other than a missed acknowledgement. Each is settled in prose by a sentence of the governing rule.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read the site, the plan, the plan's history, the maintenance agreement and the energy subscription. Work out the credit: three alarms credited, 159.50 each plus 37.50 of bundled credit, a twenty per cent step, plus 160.00 for the unwatched readings, giving 869.20; file it against the plan as a missed-acknowledgement credit, the tool periodising it to the calendar month it is filed in. Work out the labor on the world that now carries the credit: ten hours head-end plus two plus one and a half, priced at 118 less a twenty per cent discount, giving 1274.40; less 336.00 the office carries for the point map and less half the standing credit, 434.60, giving 503.80. Unlock the authorisation and hand it to the caller, who puts it through; the tool periodises the labor line to the calendar month it is booked in.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. Both computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py build_env / eval_compute / substitute) over initial_state plus the gold writes preceding each step, and the same run produced every per-factor baseline. Output (post-round-2 run): credit result=869.2, factor baselines 632.8 / 817.0 / 734.2 / 751.0 / 709.2, all-factors baseline 290.0, branches 5, history rows touched 6. Authorisation result=503.8, factor baselines 315.0 / 551.0 / 1043.8 / 742.75 / 839.8 / 938.4, all-factors baseline 1915.2, branches 7, history rows touched 16. Every factor moves the result, both all-factors baselines differ from gold, and the two figures are exactly the gold arguments at steps 8 and 10. The prerequisite sensitivity run gave: skipping step 8 leaves standing_credit at 0.00 and moves the authorised labor to 938.40.

TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE, FORWARD AND BACK. Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence that legislates it, listed in each policy's compute_basis. Back: reading each rule through, every sentence carrying a quantity, window, filter, branch, base, order or rounding semantic is claimed by a binding - the twelve-month windows by within_months, "with no acknowledgement" by the acknowledged_timestamp filter, the alarm classes by the alarm_class filters, the closure method by resolution_method, the ordering by the explicit sentences that the per-alarm credit and the bundled credit are added together before the alarms multiply them and that the subscription credit is added to the result rather than uplifted with it, and that the discount acts once on the priced hours while what the office carries and the credit are subtracted from the discounted figure in turn; the single final rounding by RND on result in both. No sentence is left unimplemented and no filter is left unstated.

POLICY - GT CLOSURE. controls_ext_alarm_ack_credit -> issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f -> computations[0] step 8 arg credit_amount_usd -> the credit row and the reduced balance. controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation -> authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b -> computations[1] step 10 arg authorised_labor_usd -> the confirmed authorisation record, the upgrade labor charge line and the raised balance. charter_scope.extended_policies equals the set of computation policy ids, required_documents repeats it in order, and charter_scope.task_tools lists the two tools in first-call order. Across the difficulty the two tasks' scopes are disjoint and together cover all five extended policies and all five tools.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the prose the two policies will be published as, the tool schemas, what the caller says and what the share lookups return: the plan is active and the tier does not include major upgrades, so the upgrade is quoted as labor; the upgrade paragraph says the labor is fixed only after every monitored alarm with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the balance, and the history shows four such alarms and no credit, so the credit must be filed first. Working the credit paragraph by hand over the six alarm rows gives 869.20; working the labor paragraph over the plan, the tickets and the two cross-product rows, with that credit standing, gives 503.80. The draft agrees with gold in the object, the order, the write sequence and both figures, and finds no second reading: the only places two readings could arise - which alarms count as credited and how much of the standing credit is set against the labor - are each settled exclusively, the first by the tier's acknowledgement target together with whether an urgent alarm stands unacknowledged, the second by whether the payments of the twelve months are at least the charges raised in them.

REVISIONS (round 1). During authoring the plan's support-hour history was cut back from the first draft so that 7.5 hours are logged against 8.0 credited: the first draft had the pool overdrawn, which would have left a support overage obligation standing in this task's world that only task 0's policy can discharge. The discount ladder, which in the first draft keyed on hours drawn against the pool, was rewritten to key on the tickets closed and the unacknowledged alarms so that it no longer depends on an overdrawn pool. Both changes were propagated to the seed, the rule, the compute, the factor ladder, the tracing and this dossier in the same pass, and the verification run above is the post-change run.


AUDIT ROUND 2 — ITEMS CLOSED AND ROUTED (audits/policy_task/controls_support_desk/_difficulty.md and 1.md).
F4 (undeclared override of base controls_software_and_security): closed inside the charter. controls_ext_upgrade_authorisation now lists controls_software_and_security in base_policy_refs and declares an overwrite of "elsewhere the upgrade is quoted, with the tier's upgrade labor discount applied, and the manufacturer's licence cost is passed through unchanged", replaced by the rule's own sentence that the labor is quoted at the hours, the rate and the discount this rule works out from the plan's records, the tier's discount being the starting point those records may raise, with the licence cost still passed through unchanged. The base readings the auditor derived (1265.80 / 1915.20) rest on the retired clause; the tier's discount remains the baseline document's default and is what the ladder starts from.
F6 (the credit tool described a nuisance-overage credit and stamped that reason): closed in task_tools.py. issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f now describes a missed-acknowledgement credit for monitored alarms the desk failed to acknowledge and stamps credit_reason missed_acknowledgement, the value the schema carries for exactly this; the unlock and call objectives in evaluation_criteria say the same. There is no longer a reading of the tool's contract under which nothing is creditable.
F7 (the maintenance row three factors read had ended by the maintenance charter's own rules): closed in the seed. The Comprehensive Performance Agreement is a 36-month tier that does not renew automatically; the row now quotes 36 months, runs 2025-07-01 to 2028-06-30, carries no renewal notice date, and stands active inside its term, so reading it by the maintenance charter and reading its status field give the same answer. No factor tier moved (the ladders read "standing active" and the tier's parameters), so the figures of round 1 that depended on it are unchanged in kind; the credit and labor figures changed for the O-1 reason below, not for this one.
SOURCE-TASK RED (billing_period of the credit not uniquely entailed): closed by removing the parameter from the agent's hands. issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f and authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b no longer take billing_period; each stamps the row with the calendar month in which it is filed or booked, stated in the tool's own docstring as its format contract. No label is left for a solver to choose; evaluation_criteria actions 8 and 10 and their tracing were updated in the same pass.
O-1 (the second tier of alarms_credited_basis was reachable only at a tier that watches no alarms): closed by re-partitioning the ladder on the tier's acknowledgement target — thirty minutes or less brings the urgent alarms in alike, longer than thirty brings in half of them taken down to a whole alarm, otherwise critical only. Every tier is now reachable by a monitored plan (Software Assurance and above sit on the first, Alarm Monitoring and Scheduled on the second, the Help Desk Subscription on the fall-through), the partition is one a monitoring desk actually draws (a tighter target promises urgent alarms the same attention as critical ones), and this world moves from the first tier to the second: the credit is now 869.20 and the labor 503.80. Every dependent figure — factor_sensitivity, baseline_result, the tracing, prerequisite_closure, this dossier — was recomputed with the gate evaluator and rewritten in the same pass.
T1-O1 (energy subscription seeded with a 24-month term on a 12-month tier): closed; the row now runs 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31, a renewed 12-month term, still active and unexpired at the handling day.
Observations judged and recorded: O-4 ("charges raised" against a count by due day) — closed charter-wide by rewording to "charges that fell due on the plan", which also touches this task's upgrade rule through the credit-offset tier ("the charges that fell due in them"); the figure is unchanged because every charge of the twelve months here fell due inside them. O-6 (energy reads owner-scoped) — left; the rule says "the owner holds" and this owner holds one subscription, at this building. O-13 (the credit and the labor line move the balance at once rather than on the next plan invoice or in the month performed) — left as a timing matter the rules state in their own words; the credit rule's opening sentence keeps base's "against its next invoice" wording as the place the credit is applied, and the tool files it now. O-14 (base treats a late acknowledgement as a missed target; the extended rule credits alarms never acknowledged) — left unexercised: the one acknowledged critical alarm here was acknowledged inside its target, so the two readings agree on this world; the rule's words "the records show with no acknowledgement" state the extended scope openly. O-9, O-10, O-11, O-12, O-15 — bear on task 0's policies or on none of this task's; see task 0's dossier.
user_scenario:
Marcus Delgado is the property manager for Ashbrook Commercial Realty, Inc. and looks after Cedar
Ridge Corporate Center among four other buildings, and he is the sort of caller who explains more than he
needs to and apologises for it. He starts by saying he has been meaning to ring for weeks. The head-end
software on the automation system at Cedar Ridge is two versions behind, his controls contractor's own
engineer told him in the spring that the version they are on is out of support, and the trend logs keep
dropping out on the workstation. What he wants today is the major software upgrade put in hand for that
building. He says straight out that he can authorise the labor himself, on this call, and that he does not
need to take it to anybody, but he is not going to commit to an open-ended number and would like to know what
the labor comes to before he says yes.

He gives the company name, Ashbrook Commercial Realty, Inc., and the office number, 3125550347, without being
asked. If the agent wants more before going into the account he reads out the account number from the top of
the last statement, 630582, and the last four of the tax identification number, 3364, one after the other.
Asked which building, it is Cedar Ridge Corporate Center out in Schaumburg. Asked what version the system is
running now he says he would have to go and look at the workstation and would rather not hold the line for
it; asked what version it ought to go to, he says that is the contractor's call, not his. Asked whether
anyone has touched the software recently, he says nobody from his side has, and as far as he knows nothing
has been loaded onto it since the plan started.

He is happy for the desk to sort out anything on the company's side of the account without checking back with
him, and says so if it comes up. Committing the money is the part he keeps: when the agent has worked out the
labor and hands him the authorisation to put through himself, he reads the figure back, says that is fine and
puts it through. If the agent tells him the figure before handing it over he takes it at face value; he has
no way of pricing controls labor and says so if he is pushed on whether it looks right. If the agent tells
him a credit has been put back on the plan he sounds mildly surprised and pleased and asks nothing further
about it.

When the agent confirms the upgrade labor is authorised and on the account, he thanks the agent, says he will
let his engineer know to expect somebody, and rings off. If the agent asks anything he genuinely cannot
answer he says so rather than guessing, and he never tells the desk what it ought to be doing.

The plan year's included support hours of 8.0 match the tier's entitlement and are credited once for 2026; 7.5 hours have been logged against resolved tickets, leaving the 0.5 the plan shows.
The plan year's included alarm responses of 24 match the tier's entitlement and are credited once for 2026; one response has been drawn, leaving the 23 the plan shows.

A critical alarm on AHU-3 raised at 02:14 on 2026-03-04 with no acknowledgement ever recorded; the tier watches alarms around the clock and targets 60 minutes, so an alarm still unacknowledged months later is a missed target rather than a timing question.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Find the owner's account from the company name and office number the caller gives, and read the profile carrying the account number, the tax identification digits and the credit standing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account can be read or written until the owner is located, and the customer reference number returned here keys every later lookup and write.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Check the two details the caller reads off his statement against the profile and record the passed verification for this call.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No credit or charge may be booked on an account until an in-session verification has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the owner's buildings so Cedar Ridge Corporate Center can be identified and its building reference number read.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The building reference is an argument of the upgrade authorisation and is what ties the automation plan, the maintenance agreement and the energy subscription to one another.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the automation service plan at that building: the tier, that it stands active, the term dates, the covered points and panels, the controller generation, the software version and the balance owed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes the alarm response overage fee, the included responses, the technician rate, the upgrade labor discount and the panel maximum; the covered panels, the covered points and the controller generation decide which tier of the head-end, hours and migration ladders applies.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the plan's history: every monitored alarm with its class and whether the desk ever acknowledged it, the responses drawn, every resolved ticket, every charge with its due day and every payment with the day it was received.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The unacknowledged alarms and the alarms raised in all decide the credit; the tickets closed, the tickets closed on site, the software updates applied and the charges and payments of the twelve months decide the head-end allowance, the hours basis, the rate, the discount and the share of the credit set against the labor.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the maintenance agreement at the same building: its tier, that it stands active, and what its tier carries.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A live maintenance agreement whose tier includes remote monitoring fixes the further credit each credited alarm carries, and whose tier covers repair labor fixes the rate the upgrade hours are priced at.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the owner's energy monitoring subscription at the building: its standing, the meters it covers and where its data comes from.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A subscription reading its data from the controls system fixes the further credit for the readings taken from the unwatched system and what the office carries for migrating the point map.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden write that files a missed-acknowledgement credit on an automation service plan for monitored alarms the desk failed to acknowledge.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this write.

evaluation_criteria.objective: File the missed-acknowledgement credit the plan is owed for the monitored alarms the desk never acknowledged, marked as such and periodised to the calendar month it is filed in, reducing the balance owed under the plan by that amount.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The missed-acknowledgement credit policy is the only rule that produces this figure, and the credit must stand on the plan's balance before the labor the owner authorises can be fixed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.plan_id: The automation service plan at Cedar Ridge Corporate Center. Basis: the plan record returned by the automation service plan lookup at action 3; the tool's contract says the reference number is 'read from the automation service plan lookup before the call'. Uniqueness: the owner holds exactly one automation service plan, so no other reference is reachable at this step.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_amount_usd: 869.20. The twelve months to 2026-09-24 carry six monitored alarms on the plan, of which AL-10004411 and AL-10004822 are critical with no acknowledgement recorded and AL-10005388 and AL-10005612 are urgent with none; AL-10005130 was acknowledged 29 minutes after it was raised and AL-10005907 18 minutes after. The tier's acknowledgement target is sixty minutes, longer than thirty, and at least one urgent alarm stands unacknowledged, so the alarms credited are the two critical ones together with half the two urgent ones taken down to a whole alarm: three. Three alarms classed as critical were raised in those twelve months and the tier includes no after-hours call-out on a critical alarm, so each credited alarm is credited at the tier's alarm response overage fee of 145 raised by ten per cent, 159.50. The building's maintenance agreement stands active and its tier includes remote monitoring of covered equipment, so a further 900 over the plan year's 24 included alarm responses, 37.50, is added for each credited alarm. Four alarms stand unacknowledged, three or more, and six monitored alarms were raised in all, fewer than ten, so the credit is raised by twenty per cent. The owner's energy subscription stands active over 8 meters and reads its data from the controls system, so one month of its 240 per-meter fee for each meter, 160.00, is added. 3 x (159.50 + 37.50) x 1.20 + 160.00 = 709.20 + 160.00, giving 869.20 rounded once to two decimal places.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the authorisation the owner gives himself and hand it over to him.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Committing money to upgrade labor is the owner's own act; the agent unlocks it at this point in the order so the caller can put it through.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The owner authorises the labor for the major controls software upgrade at his building, filing the authorisation and booking the labor on the plan.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The upgrade authorisation policy is the only rule that produces this figure, and this write is the terminal state the caller rang for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.plan_id: The automation service plan at Cedar Ridge Corporate Center. Basis: the plan record returned by the automation service plan lookup at action 3, the same reference the credit was filed against at action 8; the tool's contract says the reference number is 'read from the automation service plan lookup before the call'. Uniqueness: the owner holds exactly one automation service plan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.site_id: Cedar Ridge Corporate Center. Basis: the building record returned by the building lookup at action 2 and the same reference carried on the plan record read at action 3; the tool's contract says it is 'read from the building lookup or from the plan record before the call'. Uniqueness: the owner has one building on file with the company and the plan names that same building.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.authorised_labor_usd: 503.80. The plan covers 4 panels against the tier's maximum of 4 and the twelve months to 2026-09-24 carry one support ticket closed on site, CT-503311, so the head-end allowance is ten hours. The covered controllers are of generation 2016 against the tier's oldest supported generation of 2010, six years newer and so at least four, and no software update has been applied to the covered system in those twelve months, so the hours are ten plus half an hour for each of the 4 panels and a further half hour for each whole hundred of the 360 covered points: 10 + 2.0 + 1.5, that is 13.5 hours. The building's maintenance agreement stands active, its tier covers repair labor and a ticket was closed on site, so the hours are priced at that agreement's own regular-hours labor rate of 118 rather than the tier's 168. Four support tickets were closed in the twelve months, three or more, and four monitored alarms stand with no acknowledgement, so the tier's upgrade labor discount of 5 is raised by fifteen points to 20. 13.5 x 118 x 0.80 gives 1274.40. The owner's energy subscription stands active, reads its data from the controls system and covers 8 meters against the 6 its own tier includes, so a quarter of an hour of the tier's 168 rate for each of the 8 meters, 336.00, is carried by the office. The plan's balance carries the 869.20 credit and the payments received in the twelve months, 5460.00, are at least the charges raised in them, 5460.00, so half the credit standing, 434.60, is set against the labor. 1274.40 - 336.00 - 434.60 = 503.80, rounded once to two decimal places.

edges.condition: The plan's balance carries a credit entry for the monitored alarms the records show with no acknowledgement.
edges.policy_source: The labor the owner is asked to authorise is fixed only after every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement carries its credit on the plan's balance.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-24 the plan's balance carries no credit of any kind: of the twenty history rows, five are charge lines, two are payments, two are entitlement credits of hours and responses, six are alarms, one is an alarm response and four are resolved tickets, and none is a credit issued on the plan. Four of those alarms - AL-10004411 and AL-10004822, critical, and AL-10005388 and AL-10005612, urgent - carry no acknowledgement timestamp at all, so the state the labor waits on is plainly absent while the alarms that earn it are plainly present.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the missed-acknowledgement credit is filed the plan's history carries a credit of 869.20 marked as a missed-acknowledgement credit and the balance owed falls to -869.20, so the credit standing on the plan that the labor is worked out from becomes 869.20 rather than 0.00 and half of it, 434.60, is set against the quoted labor.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge, so there is no pair of writes that could be reordered and nothing to prove commutative. The order is forced by the value: filing the credit after the authorisation would leave the labor worked out on a balance carrying no credit, giving 938.40 instead of 503.80 and a different terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the missed-acknowledgement credit and replaying everything else leaves standing_credit at 0.00, so the credit set against the quoted labor falls from 434.60 to 0.00, the authorised labor rises from 503.80 to 938.40, and the terminal balance owed under the plan changes from -365.40 to 938.40.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller raises only the root problem, in the words 'What he wants today is the major software upgrade put in hand for that building.' He never mentions an alarm, an acknowledgement, a credit or the monitoring desk, and he drops no hint that anything might have to be sorted out first; asked why he is ringing he talks about versions and trend logs. His only line touching a credit is a reaction that can fire after the agent has raised it: 'If the agent tells him a credit has been put back on the plan he sounds mildly surprised and pleased and asks nothing further about it.' If the agent never finds the unacknowledged alarms, the caller says nothing about them.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither task tool checks a prerequisite. authorise_controls_upgrade_c5086d5b reads the plan row only to carry the customer reference and the current balance forward; it files the authorisation, books the labor charge and raises the balance by whatever amount it is given, with no branch that inspects credits and no error return. issue_controls_alarm_credit_7b85e02f files whatever credit amount it is given without looking at the alarm history. An agent that authorised the labor first would get a normal receipt and a wrong terminal hash.

factor_trace: alarms_credited_basis (method): the Alarm Monitoring Plan's acknowledgement target is sixty minutes, longer than thirty, and AL-10005388 and AL-10005612 are urgent with no acknowledgement recorded, so the alarms credited are the two critical ones together with half the two urgent ones taken down to a whole alarm, three in all; the standard method credits only the two unacknowledged critical alarms and would have given 632.80.

per_alarm_credit_unit (parameter): AL-10004411, AL-10004822 and AL-10005130 make three alarms classed as critical in the twelve months, and the Alarm Monitoring Plan includes no after-hours call-out on a critical alarm, so each credited alarm is credited at 159.50 rather than the tier's plain 145; at the plain fee the credit would be 817.00.

bundled_monitoring_credit (parameter): the building's Comprehensive Performance Agreement stands active and its tier includes remote monitoring of covered equipment, so a further 37.50 is added for each credited alarm, being its 900 annual credit for holding an automation plan over the plan year's 24 included responses; with no further credit the figure would be 734.20.

repeated_missed_acknowledgement_step (parameter): four alarms stand with no acknowledgement, three or more, and six monitored alarms were raised in all, fewer than ten, so the credit is raised by twenty per cent; with no step it would be 751.00.

unwatched_reading_credit (parameter): the owner's Metering & Dashboard Subscription stands active over eight meters and reads its data from the controls system, so one month of its 240 per-meter fee for each meter, 160.00, is added; with no such credit the figure would be 709.20.
bindings belonging to no factor: unacked_total and result are the arithmetic that assembles the count and the final sum.

factor_trace: head_end_allowance (parameter): the plan covers four panels against the tier's maximum of four and CT-503311 was closed on site in the twelve months, so the head-end allowance is ten hours rather than twelve; at the standard eight the labor would be 315.00.

upgrade_hours_basis (method): the covered controllers are of generation 2016 against the tier's oldest supported generation of 2010, and no software update has been applied in the twelve months, so the hours are the head-end allowance plus half an hour for each of the four panels and a further half hour for each whole hundred of the 360 points: 13.5; the standard method of one hour a panel gives 14 hours and a labor figure of 551.00.

upgrade_labor_rate (parameter): the Comprehensive Performance Agreement stands active, covers repair labor, and a ticket was closed on site, so the hours are priced at its own labor rate of 118; at the tier's 168 the labor would be 1043.80.

deferred_upgrade_discount (parameter): four support tickets were closed in the twelve months, three or more, and four monitored alarms stand with no acknowledgement, so the tier's upgrade labor discount of 5 is raised by fifteen points to 20; at the tier's plain discount the labor would be 742.75.

point_map_migration_carried (parameter): the energy subscription stands active, reads from the controls system and covers eight meters against the six its own tier includes, so a quarter of an hour of the tier's 168 rate for each meter, 336.00, is carried by the office; with nothing carried the labor would be 839.80.

standing_credit_offset_share (parameter): the plan's balance carries the 869.20 credit and the payments of the twelve months, 5460.00, are at least the charges that fell due in them, 5460.00, so half the credit, 434.60, is set against the labor; with none set against it the labor would be 938.40.

bindings belonging to no factor: point_blocks, quoted_labor, standing_credit and result are the per-hundred-point arithmetic, the priced hours, the plain aggregate of the credits standing on the plan and the final sum.
